Active-route derivation (web NavLink computes isActive from the router match) has no native router, so it is bridged: isActive prop overrides; otherwise deriveIsActive compares currentPath against `to` with normalizePath (trailing-slash trim) doing exact match when `end` is set and a segment-boundary prefix match otherwise, approximating react-router NavLink matching. isPending/isTransitioning are router transition states with no native equivalent and are always false (documented).

Native-safe guard context: NavigationGuardContextValue exposes only confirmIfDirty (the single member a link uses; the web provider's register is not needed here). NOOP_NAVIGATION_GUARD.confirmIfDirty resolves true, mirroring the web NOOP_CTX so links render and navigate inside isolated tests without a provider. NavigationGuardContext + useNavigationGuardContext are exported so a future native NavigationGuardProvider port (or a host/test) can supply a real confirmIfDirty; a per-call confirmIfDirty prop override is also accepted.

Explicit native reductions (all documented in the file header): (1) react-router <Link>/<NavLink>/useNavigate -> Pressable + onNavigate bridge; without a bridge a confirmed press is a no-op navigation. (2) MouseEvent modifier-key and middle-click skip branches are DOM-only and dropped; only the target skip survives. (3) confirmIfDirty comes from the inline native NavigationGuardContext (no-op default) until NavigationGuardProvider is ported. (4) NavLink isActive is host-driven via isActive/currentPath; isPending/isTransitioning are always false. runGuardedNavigation swallows guard rejections (web leaves them unhandled) so a misbehaving host guard cannot crash the press handler.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, react-router-dom, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, lucide-react, or old web @/components/ui imports in the native output -- only react and react-native primitives.
